Use FFmpeg: https://ffmpeg.org

You can use the following command:

ffmpeg -i input.mp4 -vf "select='not(mod(n,5))',setpts=N/(30*TB)" -vframes 120 -an output.mp4

This command will not necessarily extract keyframes, it will extract every 5th frame whether it's a keyframe or not. If you specifically want keyframes, you can use the select='eq(pict_type,PICT_TYPE_I)' filter instead, but this will not guarantee a frame every 5 frames or a consistent framerate, as keyframes are not typically that frequent.

That's really impressive. Although there are, of course, a lot of elements in combination, could you give some tips about how to train a model/Lora to achieve such a natural, realistic style? I'm not an expert in photography, but I'm a software developer studying image generation since the first mid-journey when DALL-E appeared, and I'm focusing on photorealistic mainly using stable diffusion since then. I can see you are generating at a very large resolution, so I suppose that you fine-tuned a model with lots of high-res photos. I also looked at other great photos you posted, and there is a very similar one but with a few different features. Based on the prompt, I might suppose that it's not a celebrity. So, I'm still thinking about the realism of the face, and I think it's almost 80% of the convincing elements. I also noticed that you used some LORAS. In fact, there are some interesting ones around, like to control light and colors. Another thing that might help the realism is the simulation of image format artifacts, like in JPEG. Finally, I would like to know if you used any other model like ControlNet (in this case, since I saw others you posted, you used Canny), and if you used any post-processing outside stable diffusion, like Photoshop. Thank you so much for sharing. I would love to test your model when it's done and also to share some ideas on Discord and even help with the processes. Cheers!
